summary:
Echoes in the Dust is an interactive digital storybook and field guide created to introduce school-age space enthusiasts to NASA's historic hardware resting across the Moon, Mars, and deep space.

 The project brings "abandoned" equipment—such as the Apollo 11 Eagle descent stage, the Opportunity rover, the InSight lander, and Voyager 1—back to life through engaging narrative storytelling and official mission photography, mapping out the physical machines left behind alongside the planetary science they achieved.

It transforms complex space exploration history into accessible, captivating educational content, sparking curiosity and inspiring the next generation of scientists and space explorers to appreciate the lasting legacy of human ingenuity across the solar system.
details: Echoes in the Dust is an interactive digital field guide and presentation deck designed to introduce school-age space enthusiasts to NASA’s historic hardware resting across the Moon, Mars, and deep space. It brings abandoned equipment—such as the Apollo 11 Eagle descent stage, lunar rovers, the Opportunity rover, the InSight lander, and the Voyager 1 spacecraft—back to life through engaging narrative storytelling. The project guides users through each artifact's historical location, mission status, and the specific scientific breakthroughs it unlocked. Its primary benefit is making space science accessible, educational, and captivating for young learners, with the intended impact of sparking curiosity about planetary science, preserving the legacy of historic space missions, and inspiring the next generation of engineers and scientists. The project was developed using Gamma AI for visual layout and slide generation, supported by official open data from the NASA Image and Video Library, the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC), and the Planetary Data System (PDS). The team focused on human-centric storytelling to transform silent metal relics into monuments of human curiosity while adhering strictly to project guidelines, presentation limits, and official data citations
